items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: An actively exploited Check Point vulnerability has been added to the KEV, requiring immediate attention for SOC and incident response teams.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-123039, an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability affecting multiple Check Point products, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. The addition is based on evidence of active exploitation, making it a priority for remediation under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04. Federal agencies are required to prioritize patching this vulnerability on publicly exposed assets, as it can grant total control of the system post-exploitation. CISA also encourages private organizations to adopt this risk-based management approach to mitigate potential breaches.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-123039 is now confirmed to be under active exploitation, and organizations using Check Point products must prioritize its remediation.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

items.title: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical command injection flaw in UnrealIRCd is being actively exploited, requiring immediate remediation.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-114713, an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability in UnrealIRCd, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog. The flaw allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands, which are then executed with server authority. Federal agencies are required to apply mitigations by November 16, 2026. This vulnerability poses a significant risk of unauthorized command execution across linked IRC infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Organizations running UnrealIRCd must patch CVE-2026-114713 immediately to prevent unauthorized users from executing commands with full server authority.

items.title: Hackers compromise 4,800 GitHub accounts to steal cloud credentials
items.one_liner: A sweeping GitHub credential-theft campaign dubbed 'wfx-loot' has compromised nearly 4,800 accounts to harvest cloud secrets from over 60,000 repositories.
items.summary: Threat actors launched a campaign dubbed 'wfx-loot' on GitHub, compromising 4,837 user accounts to probe 61,764 repositories, open automated pull requests, and deploy secrets-stealing malware. The attacks leveraged automated workflows to harvest credentials, tokens, and configuration files from enterprise and open-source environments.
items.bottom_line: Compromised developer accounts can be weaponized at scale via automated workflows to systematically pillage cloud credentials across thousands of code repositories.

items.title: CVE-2026-119618: What We Know About the Critical Apache mod_http2 Race Condition
items.one_liner: Critical HTTP/2 race condition CVE-2026-119618 in Apache allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: The Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-119618, a critical race condition in the mod_http2 module affecting Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The flaw arises from improper synchronization in the assign_headers() function, leading to heap memory corruption and potential unauthenticated remote code execution. Red Hat reports that public research has demonstrated reliable exploitation against default configurations. The issue is resolved in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71.

Affected versions: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70
items.bottom_line: Upgrade Apache HTTP Server immediately to version 2.4.71 to patch an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability in mod_http2.

items.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
items.one_liner: Newly disclosed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell flaws in N-able N-central enable root and SYSTEM RCE on patched servers.
items.summary: Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed new proof-of-concept exploits codenamed 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell targeting N-able N-central on-premise version 2026.4 HF2. The vulnerabilities affect non-default configurations where the Legacy API is exposed: 4EverAble2Shell enables unauthenticated remote code execution as root, while Agent2Shell permits command execution as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on managed Windows agents. Threat intelligence providers observed immediate probing activity against CVE-2026-90436 and 4EverAble2Shell following public disclosures, prompting N-able to strongly urge users to disable the Legacy API immediately.

items.title: ZDI-26-964: (Pwn2Own) Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE in Philips Hue Bridge allows nearby attackers to compromise the smart home hub.
items.summary: A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been disclosed in the Philips Hue Bridge, affecting the HomeKit Accessory Protocol (HAP) service. The flaw, discovered during Pwn2Own, is an integer underflow that occurs when the service parses pairing requests on TCP port 8080. Network-adjacent attackers can exploit this without authentication to execute arbitrary code on the device. A fix has been released in Bridge v2 software version 1975170000.

items.title: CVE-2026-0324 GlobalProtect App: Incorrect Privilege Management Vulnerability in OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK on Windows (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: This vulnerability is critical for your Windows endpoint security work as it provides a direct path for local privilege escalation via a common security tool.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed a medium-severity privilege escalation vulnerability in the GlobalProtect app for Windows. The flaw originates in the integrated OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK and allows a locally authenticated non-administrative user to gain NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges. No special configuration is required for exposure, though Palo Alto Networks reports no known exploitation in the wild. The issue is resolved by updating to GlobalProtect versions that include MetaDefender SDK 4.3.4822 or later.
items.bottom_line: Local users on Windows systems running vulnerable GlobalProtect versions can escalate to full SYSTEM privileges due to a flaw in the third-party OPSWAT SDK.

items.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
items.one_liner: This massive outage highlights the fragility of global cloud infrastructure and the cascading impact of routine network upgrades.
items.summary: Microsoft has fully restored its global services following a massive outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for over 430 million users across 70 countries. The company attributed the nearly 24-hour disruption to a 'network capacity upgrade' rather than a cyberattack or AI-related failure. The outage impacted critical infrastructure, including the Japanese government, North American hospitals, and the Australian spy agency. While services began recovering on Friday afternoon, the event caused significant delays in business operations and personal transactions globally.
items.bottom_line: A routine network capacity upgrade by Microsoft triggered a 24-hour global outage affecting 430 million users and critical government services.

items.title: CVE-2026-64678 (CRITICAL 9.8): NOsql Object (NO2 a.k.a Nitrite) database is an open source nosql embedded document store. Prior to version 4…
items.one_liner: Upgrade Nitrite embedded database to version 4.4.1 immediately to patch a critical Java deserialization RCE vulnerability.
items.summary: NOsql Object (Nitrite) database versions prior to 4.4.1 contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-64678, CVSS 9.8) involving unsafe deserialization. When automatically migrating legacy v1-format stores, Nitrite passes raw deserialized bytes directly to java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject() via a custom subclass without any class allowlist, blocklist, or ObjectInputFilter. Consequently, an attacker can instantiate any Serializable class on the classpath, leading to remote code execution if a suitable gadget chain is present. The vulnerability has been resolved in version 4.4.1.
items.bottom_line: Unsafe Java deserialization during legacy database migration in Nitrite versions prior to 4.4.1 permits unauthenticated remote code execution.

The fixes include a critical integer overflow in the regular expression compiler, high-severity issues in OAuth/OIDC discovery and OmniAuth-to-LDAP auto-linking, and several medium and low severity bugs. Installations not using official packages with bundled runtimes must also upgrade Ruby to version 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later to mitigate CVE-2026-110264. items.title: US blames system upgrade for longest nationwide FAA ground stop since 9/11
items.one_liner: A faulty router upgrade by defense contractor L3Harris caused a rare nationwide US FAA ground stop affecting thousands of flights.
items.summary: A nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop, the longest since September 11, was triggered by routine router maintenance performed by contractor L3Harris at a remote location. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that a contractor error or a faulty router caused the equipment to flood the air traffic control network with thousands of connection attempts every few seconds. The resulting disruption in radar feeds and pilot communications forced officials to halt all domestic air traffic for safety reasons. Government officials confirmed there was no evidence of a cyberattack or malicious activity. The incident affected 12,000 flights and resulted in thousands of cancellations as airlines worked to recover schedule integrity.
items.bottom_line: A contractor network maintenance error flooded air traffic control systems, causing the longest US nationwide aviation ground stop since 9/11.

items.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
items.one_liner: SilentAir exploited hacked telecom equipment in Asia using SS7 and Diameter signaling to intercept 2FA codes.
items.summary: A state-level spying group named SilentAir hacked equipment inside mobile operators across at least six Asian countries to intercept SMS 2FA codes and calls, primarily targeting individuals in Taiwan. Security firm Enea discovered that the attackers exploited SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols by sending fraudulent UpdateLocation messages via compromised IPX network infrastructure. The operations occurred in intermittent bursts since early 2025 and targeted various government and political VIPs. Enea has notified the affected operators, though it remains unclear whether the compromised equipment has been cleaned.
items.bottom_line: Compromised operator equipment allows state-level actors to silently intercept mobile calls and 2FA codes via SS7 and Diameter signaling.

items.one_liner: ZDI-26-984 in TrendAI Vision One Security Agent allows local attackers to achieve SYSTEM execution via a heap buffer overflow.
items.summary: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, designated ZDI-26-984, affects the TMBMServer component of the TrendAI Vision One Security Agent. The flaw stems from insufficient length validation of user-supplied data prior to memory copying within the Trend Micro Unauthorized Change Prevention Service. A local attacker possessing low-privileged code execution rights can exploit this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges. TrendAI has released software updates to resolve the security issue.

items.title: North Korea ‘s Crypto Theft Operations: DOJ Seizes $1.2 Billion and Disrupts Hacker Infrastructure
items.one_liner: North Korean hackers are using AI deepfakes to target open-source developers and steal billions in cryptocurrency.
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has seized over $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency and disrupted infrastructure used by North Korean hackers in the 'FaceStealer' social engineering scheme. The campaign, linked to actors like BlueNoroff and APT38, uses AI-generated deepfakes and stolen accounts to trick open-source developers and crypto professionals into installing malware during fake meetings. Hackers often wait months after initial compromise before stealing funds or taking control of repositories. The DOJ also recovered funds tied to a massive $6 billion Binance theft from October 2026.
items.bottom_line: The use of AI-driven social engineering to target open-source maintainers represents a sophisticated shift in North Korean cyber operations, necessitating heightened vigilance during remote interactions.

items.title: Maersk Reveals Data Breach as Extortion Group Demands $5m
items.one_liner: A legacy system breach at Maersk highlights the persistent security risks inherent in M&A activity and inherited infrastructure.
items.summary: Shipping giant Maersk has confirmed a data breach after the WhiteArmor extortion group claimed to have stolen 100GB of data. The incident involved a legacy system from a previous acquisition and allegedly includes driver records, plaintext passwords, and mobile device logs. WhiteArmor is demanding a $5 million ransom in Bitcoin and has recently targeted other logistics firms like J.B. Hunt and Ryder. Maersk states that no sensitive data has been disclosed and customer platforms remain operational.
items.bottom_line: Maersk's breach by the WhiteArmor group serves as a warning that legacy systems from acquisitions remain high-value targets for data-theft extortionists.

items.title: CVE-2026-126173 - AutomatorWP Pro Webhooks addon <= 1.4.4 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary User Password Reset / Account Takeover via Webhook with 'Is the user ID' Field
items.one_liner: Audit and patch AutomatorWP Pro Webhooks addon to version > 1.4.4 to prevent unauthenticated account takeover via webhooks.
items.summary: The AutomatorWP Pro Webhooks addon up to version 1.4.4 suffers from a missing authorization vulnerability (CVE-2026-126173) that permits unauthenticated attackers to trigger arbitrary user password resets and complete account takeovers. The flaw occurs when an administrator configures a specific supported pairing involving a Receive Webhook trigger with an 'Is the user ID' field mapped to an Update-User action with a blank User ID field. Unauthenticated actors can exploit this misconfiguration to hijack administrative accounts.
items.bottom_line: An authorization bypass in AutomatorWP Pro Webhooks addon <= 1.4.4 allows unauthenticated attackers to take over administrator accounts via crafted webhook requests.

items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. A security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, enabling anyone to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds. Cisco issued an informational security advisory regarding the emergency distrust of these eMudhra root and intermediate certificate authorities across products. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks Out-of-Band Blind XML External Entity Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical XML external entity injection vulnerability in Cisco BroadWorks allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to exfiltrate sensitive configuration files.
items.summary: Cisco BroadWorks contains a critical vulnerability in its Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration files. Attackers can exploit this by sending a crafted XML message to the OCI-P service, potentially gaining access to sensitive filesystem data. Cisco has released software updates to address this issue, and there are no available workarounds.

items.title: ZDI-26-1002: Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Qdisc Improper Validation of Array Index Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A Linux kernel array index validation flaw in taprio_enqueue allows local attackers to achieve privilege escalation.
items.summary: A local privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the Linux Kernel Net Scheduler Qdisc due to improper validation of array indexes in the taprio_enqueue function. A low-privileged local attacker can exploit the lack of proper bounds checking to trigger a write past the end of an allocated array, allowing them to execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Linux has released an upstream code commit to resolve the flaw.

items.bottom_line: The nationwide flight grounding underscores the urgent need for infrastructure modernization, as current systems remain highly susceptible to single-point failures during maintenance.

items.one_liner: A critical cryptographic vulnerability in the 'create-ecdh' library allows private key recovery via invalid-curve attacks.
items.summary: The 'create-ecdh' library, a browser-compatible implementation of Node.js crypto, is vulnerable to invalid-curve attacks in versions 4.0.4 and below. While modern Node.js environments using native crypto are unaffected, applications relying on the JavaScript fallback are at risk. The issue has been patched in version 4.0.5.
items.bottom_line: Developers using 'create-ecdh' in browser environments or older Node.js versions must update to 4.0.5 immediately to prevent potential private key compromise.

items.title: Open WebUI: the Windows installer mints the master key from the install second — CVE-2025-15603 was rejected; here is the measurement
items.one_liner: Open WebUI's Windows installer uses a weak, predictable seed for its master secret key, allowing full session token forgery.
items.summary: The Windows installer for Open WebUI generates a master secret key using a linear congruential generator seeded only by the installation time in seconds. This flaw allows an attacker to recover the master key in approximately 2.1 seconds, enabling the forgery of administrator session tokens. Despite being reported as CVE-2025-15603, the vendor disputed the finding and rejected the CVE, claiming no action was required. New research confirms the vulnerability persists across all 178 release tags, with most lacking even basic per-account session stamps.

items.bottom_line: Administrators should assume all Open WebUI installations on Windows are compromised and rotate all secrets immediately.

items.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
items.one_liner: MemCredit improves long-horizon web agent memory management by prioritizing decision utility over semantic relevance.
items.summary: Large language model agents handling long web interaction histories struggle because semantically relevant memories do not always improve decision utility. To address this, researchers introduced MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that estimates the state-, context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories via counterfactual interventions. MemCredit condenses these credits into a lightweight utility estimator, using semantic relevance solely for initial candidate generation under a fixed token budget. Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop, MemCredit achieved an 86.57 SR@50 under a 500-token memory budget, outperforming traditional BM25 retrieval. The findings indicate that decision utility provides a more effective principle than semantic relevance for managing agent memory.
items.bottom_line: Decision-centric memory selection via counterfactual credit estimation significantly outperforms semantic retrieval in long-horizon LLM agents.

claims.text: We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility.

items.title: Where Autonomy Belongs: A Separation of Powers for Agentic Program Evolution
items.one_liner: Adopt EvoTrias's separation-of-powers architecture to build more reliable, cost-efficient LLM coding agents.
items.summary: LLM-driven program evolution struggles due to misallocated autonomy across govern, propose, and judge decisions, capping proposal scope and benchmark reliability. To fix this, researchers introduce EvoX or rather EvoTrias, a separation-of-powers architecture that assigns Structured Governance, Open Proposal, and Protected Judgment to distinct owners communicating through typed contracts and runtime hooks. Applied to benchmarks, EvoTrias cuts token costs by 64%, extends evolution to a 680K-line industrial repository, and sets new state-of-the-art results on algorithm-design tasks.
items.bottom_line: Separating governance, proposal, and judgment into isolated owners in LLM program evolution drastically cuts token costs and improves benchmark reliability.

claims.text: We address this problem with EvoTrias, a separation-of-powers architecture in which each decision has one owner: Structured Governance for what spans evolution rounds, Open Proposal for construction inside a task, and Protected Judgment behind a private evaluator.

items.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
items.one_liner: Implement DISCERN's write-time bi-temporal graph and read-time resolution framework to drastically improve LLM agent memory accuracy.
items.summary: Enterprise LLM agents struggle with memory over multi-session interactions because standard RAG treats retention as a retrieval problem instead of an entity resolution and currency challenge. The authors introduce DISCERN (Disambiguation and Cross-session Episodic memory Navigation), which preserves data at write time via a bi-temporal provenance graph and resolves ambiguities at read time using a zero-LLM tool surface driven by an agentic loop. Evaluated on ENT-310 and LoCoMo corpora, DISCERN outperforms baselines by achieving a 0.924 abstention F1 score and superior macro answer correctness through robust entity resolution.
items.bottom_line: DISCERN solves enterprise LLM agent memory conflicts by preserving raw provenance at write and using zero-LLM graph navigation for precise entity resolution at read.

The authors introduce SynthCorp, a platform that synthesizes customizable corporate data estates containing relational databases, document stores, and data catalogs by simulating how business events modify data over time. The platform generates evaluation tasks and extracts verified gold programs directly from simulation logs. Initial benchmarks generated via SynthCorp comprise seven data estates and 256 tasks, effectively exposing reasoning failures in state-of-the-art enterprise data agents.
items.bottom_line: SynthCorp automates the creation of complex corporate data estates and verifiable benchmarks to expose reasoning gaps in enterprise data agents.

items.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
items.one_liner: Together AI's TKCC is a continual compilation framework that optimizes AI inference, outperforming frontier engines by up to 2.6x.
items.summary: Together AI introduced Together Compiler (TKCC), a continual agent loop designed to optimize AI inference workloads amidst rapidly changing model architectures and traffic distributions. To overcome the throughput-fidelity tradeoff in agent optimization, TKCC utilizes a Tiered Persistent Engine to decouple engine launch overheads from forward-pass computation alongside a specialized cost model for parallel configuration. TKCC outperforms highly-optimized hand-written Megakernels by up to 1.7x on the Llama 1B workload and beats open-source engines on frontier models like Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash by up to 2.6x higher tokens per second. The system currently serves trillions of tokens across Together AI's production fleet.
key_facts: Frontier Model Improvement: Up to 2.6x TPS
items.bottom_line: Together Compiler successfully resolves the inference throughput-fidelity tradeoff through continual agent optimization, setting state-of-the-art TPS records across frontier models.

items.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
items.one_liner: Integrate EvoX's Rust-based operational policy runtime into your multi-model agent stack to improve tool-use reliability.
items.summary: Large language model agents frequently fail in tool execution due to mismatches and workflow interruptions. Researchers present EvoX, a Rust-based, multi-model agent runtime guided by 'The Second Policy,' which treats the agent harness as an Operational Policy complementing the model's Semantic Policy. EvoX integrates deterministic runtime control through Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. Evaluated across five benchmarks and six foundation models, EvoX achieves a top numerical success rate of 56.2%, demonstrating strong cross-provider adaptability without requiring external memory or complex extensions.
items.bottom_line: Treating agent harnesses as operational runtime policies via EvoX significantly increases agent execution success rates across diverse foundation models.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
items.one_liner: LLMON is an XML-like markup language designed to defeat prompt injection and replace brittle JSON parsing in LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced LLMON (LLM Object Notation), an LLM-native markup language designed to replace JSON for causal language models by using reserved special-token delimiters for explicit structure and data binding. By wrapping semantic components in tags and mapping unique identifiers to instructions, the format prevents indirect prompt injections and stops models from pulling unrelated context into answers. IBM has released two experimental preview models based on Granite 4.1 (3B and 8B parameters) trained natively on LLMON, alongside a GitHub toolkit for conversions and workflows.
items.bottom_line: Adopting LLMON and its supporting Granite models eliminates indirect prompt injection risks by explicitly binding instructions to data payloads.

items.summary: A high-severity heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability, CVE-2026-63660 with an 8.1 CVSS score, impacts the node-fontnik font rendering library prior to version 0.7.7. items.bottom_line: Upgrade node-fontnik to version 0.7.7 to prevent integer overflow and heap out-of-bounds writes from crafted font files.

items.title: Screen Eavesdropping Over the Air: Open-Source Deep-TEMPEST Tool on GitHub Uses AI to Read HDMI Cable Signals - Andro-News
items.one_liner: Deep-TEMPEST lets attackers passively reconstruct text from HDMI cable RF emissions using SDRs and PyTorch, bypassing air-gapped security.
items.summary: Researchers at the University of the Republic in Montevideo published Deep-TEMPEST on GitHub, an open-source tool that uses Software-Defined Radio (SDR) and deep learning to reconstruct live monitor output from unintended radio emissions leaking out of ordinary HDMI cables. Operating completely passively and without network access or malware, the tool tunes into the third pixel harmonic (such as 324 MHz in 1600x900 tests) using hardware like HackRF, passes raw frames through GNU Radio and the DRUNet PyTorch architecture for denoising, and applies Tesseract OCR. This pipeline reduces the character error rate from gr-tempest's 90% down to under 30%, making onscreen text legible to humans or language models from afar.
key_facts: Center frequency: 324 MHz (third harmonic of pixel clock in 1600x900 tests)
items.bottom_line: Deep-TEMPEST demonstrates that deep learning and SDRs can passively read monitor output via stray HDMI cable radio emissions with under 30% character error.

items.title: CVE-2011-10042: HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached
items.one_liner: A memcached command injection vulnerability in older Perl HTTP::Session versions allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands via crafted session IDs.
items.summary: A vulnerability (CVE-2011-10042) has been identified in HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl, allowing memcached command injection. The flaw exists because the session ID from a client cookie is passed to memcached as a cache key without proper filtering. An attacker can inject CR and LF characters into the session ID to terminate the cache command early and execute arbitrary memcached commands. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.43 or later, or migrate to an alternative like Plack::Middleware::Session.
items.bottom_line: Applications using outdated versions of HTTP::Session are at risk of memcached command injection and should be updated or migrated immediately.

items.title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
items.one_liner: A multi-agent negotiation tournament reveals that LLMs and isolated reinforcement-learning policies fail under shifting market scarcity compared to robust runtime architectures.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a competitive tournament testing nine negotiation architectures across rule-based, search, optimization, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families in a two-sided Gale-Shapley matching market under varying supply and demand scarcity conditions. The study found that reinforcement-learning agents struggled with match rates when demand shifted against them unless trained specifically against rival agents, though train/deployment mismatches still affected payoff. Nine large language models ranging from 1 to 72 billion parameters were tested under the same protocol and lost significantly to the strongest engines in 32 of 36 comparisons, winning none. The results demonstrate that isolated evaluations can hide critical failure modes in multi-agent bargaining systems.
items.bottom_line: Evaluating AI agents in isolated duels is insufficient; multi-agent tournaments reveal that LLMs and naive RL policies suffer severe performance drops under shifting market scarcity.

items.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
items.one_liner: Research challenges the assumption that forcing AI agents to align beliefs with self-assessments improves self-correction, noting it can degrade reasoning competence.
items.summary: This research paper explores epistemic akrasia in AI agents, examining whether self-assessing an agent's reasoning as defective should always compel it to abandon its conclusions. The analysis challenges the core assumption that achieving full agreement between an agent's conclusions and its self-evaluation necessarily improves its self-correction capabilities.
items.bottom_line: Enforcing strict agreement between an agent's conclusions and its self-assessments can paradoxically worsen its ability to correct mistakes.

items.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
items.one_liner: Rewriting LLM problem statements using targeted methods like decomposition can boost accuracy, but mismatched rewrites degrade performance.
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether large language models benefit from problem statement reformulation prior to solving complex math, logic, and code tasks. They tested three types of rewrites: decomposition, typed reformulation, and concept reduction, across eight models and eight benchmarks. While an oracle picking the best rewrite post-hoc increased accuracy by an average of 27.6%, no single rewrite strategy helped every problem type. Mismatched rewrites frequently degraded performance, but simple fixed rules learned from one dataset successfully transferred gains to new problems, yielding an 11.0% improvement on chosen problems. The findings demonstrate that rewriting is conditional rather than a universal problem-solving solution.

items.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
items.one_liner: Guardscope provides a necessary security audit tool for developers to verify if their LLM agent gateways are actually catching all malicious actions.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced 'guardscope,' a framework designed to measure the effectiveness of runtime controls, such as agent gateways, in LLM agent systems. The framework addresses the gap where agents can bypass controls by acting through paths other than standard tool-call channels. Guardscope uses a static stage to predict which of 15 action paths a control can check and an empirical stage that reconciles control decisions against kernel-level ground truth. Experiments with Microsoft's agent governance toolkit and other gateways demonstrate that guardscope can verify a control's coverage claims under a kernel-verified protocol.

items.bottom_line: Guardscope allows developers to verify the actual coverage of LLM agent security controls by comparing them against kernel-level ground truth.

items.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
items.one_liner: SkillEarth enables general-purpose agents to autonomously learn and refine remote sensing tool-call skills without requiring model retraining.
items.summary: SkillEarth is a new self-evolving skill extraction method designed to equip general-purpose agents with remote sensing (RS) tool-call knowledge. By externalizing knowledge into reusable, evolvable skill files, the method allows agents to adapt to new tools and tasks without retraining or parameter updates. SkillEarth uses 'dual-judge feedback' and a 'grounded observation routing graph' to refine skills at the component level based on real tool-chain execution. Experiments show that SkillEarth improves tool selection, argument correctness, and task completion across various LLMs compared to existing methods.
items.bottom_line: SkillEarth provides a scalable, training-free approach for agents to master complex remote sensing workflows through continuous, observation-grounded skill evolution.

items.title: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
items.one_liner: AutoAssumption uses formal proofs to automatically discover and optimize ML system algorithms by challenging their core assumptions.
items.summary: Researchers have developed 'AutoAssumption,' a harness that automates the discovery of machine learning system algorithms by searching over their underlying assumptions. By formalizing 89 existing algorithms as proof graphs in Lean, the tool can relax specific assumptions to derive and prove new, optimized versions. In testing, AutoAssumption produced state-of-the-art results for KV-cache eviction and weight pruning, outperforming published methods. This approach turns algorithm design into a structured search space, potentially accelerating innovation in ML systems.
items.bottom_line: Automating the search for algorithmic improvements via formal verification can produce state-of-the-art ML optimizations that human researchers might overlook.

items.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
items.one_liner: Using LLMs for causal discovery shows promise but currently lacks the reliability required for robust, automated causal graph construction.
items.summary: Researchers are investigating the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide semantic priors for causal discovery, a process often hindered by unresolved or unstable causal directions. The study evaluates three key decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Findings indicate that while semantic information improves recovery over random orientations, current methods for admission and retention are unreliable, with learned references containing the true DAG in only three of 80 tasks. The research highlights significant limitations in calibration size and reference adequacy.
items.bottom_line: The integration of semantic priors from LLMs into causal discovery is currently limited by unreliable admission and retention mechanisms, necessitating better calibration.

items.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
items.one_liner: WordInferBench evaluates coding agents on inferring Word document formatting edits from context rather than explicit instructions.
items.summary: Researchers introduced WordInferBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether autonomous agents can infer document-editing attributes from context rather than relying on explicit instructions. The benchmark comprises 280 base document-editing instances across three instruction conditions: descriptive, referential, and inferential. Testing six recent coding-agent systems revealed a significant performance drop when formatting changes had to be determined from document context. Specifically, Claude Code with Opus 4.6 achieved a 62.9% task-level pass rate on descriptive variants but only 40.7% on inferential variants, highlighting current limitations in contextual attribute inference.

items.title: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
items.one_liner: Understand that cleaning an AI agent's error history without fixing the underlying environment state degrades subsequent performance.
items.summary: Researchers studied how editing tool-using language-model agent histories affects task recovery when errors persist in the environment. Using AgentCE-Bench and AppWorld, they found that adding truthful explanatory notes next to preserved errors raised receiver recovery from 51% to 66%, while presenting completed actions or contradictory database receipts lowered task success rates. The findings demonstrate that a history edited to look clean while the environment still holds an error can leave an agent worse off than unedited histories. This highlights the critical dependency between agent conversation history and the actual world state.
items.bottom_line: Making an AI agent's history look clean while errors persist in the real environment significantly harms task recovery and success.

items.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
items.one_liner: Frontier LLMs replicate human-like temporal inference in social coordination games but fail to adapt dynamically to partners over time.
items.summary: Researchers investigated how humans and AI use implicit temporal cues—such as pause durations—for social coordination by evaluating 150 humans alongside computer-use agents and standard LLMs in a cooperative card game called The Mind. The study found that human behavior matches a Bayesian strategy inferring partners' mental states from timing cues, a capability also exhibited by frontier AI models. However, unlike humans, the tested models failed to efficiently adapt their behavior to specific partners over repeated interactions. The findings point to challenges for AI systems in dynamically interpreting and adapting to implicit human timing signals.

items.bottom_line: While frontier AI models can perform probabilistic timing inferences, they currently lack the dynamic partner adaptation seen in humans during social coordination.

items.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
items.one_liner: Coding agents solve tasks early but continue executing unnecessary steps, occasionally undoing their correct patches.
items.summary: A study across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets characterized 'termination lag'—the number of steps coding agents execute after generating their first correct patch. Researchers found that while 38–82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit, agents continue working for substantial periods, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35–60% of successful runs. Agents spend these extra steps verifying work and exploring repositories, though in 1–8% of cases, this continued activity causes them to undo their correct patch.

Runs where continued activity undid correct patch: 1–8%
items.bottom_line: Coding agents frequently suffer from termination lag, continuing to execute steps long after finding correct solutions and occasionally breaking their working code.

items.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale
items.one_liner: Agent Substrate is a CNCF Sandbox runtime designed to scale Kubernetes for idle-heavy AI agents.
items.summary: Agent Substrate is an open-source, zero-trust runtime donated to the CNCF Sandbox to address Kubernetes' inefficiencies when running autonomous AI agents and coding assistants at scale. Because traditional Kubernetes Pod lifecycles introduce multi-second cold starts and hold idle memory, Agent Substrate multiplexes many agent sessions across a smaller pool of persistent worker Pods. Idle sessions are snapshotted—including memory and filesystems via gVisor or microVMs—and restored onto available workers without hitting the API server or scheduler. This architecture achieves tenfold higher density and eliminates the latency overhead of turning agent steps into ephemeral containers.

items.bottom_line: Agent Substrate solves the container cold-start and memory overhead problem for AI agents on Kubernetes by checkpointing and multiplexing sessions over worker pools.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
items.one_liner: LLM verifiers dramatically improve math accuracy but at the cost of rejecting the vast majority of attempts.
items.summary: This research evaluates 'certify-or-decline' verification for mathematical reasoning in open-weight LLMs. The study found that while certification significantly boosts precision—by 46 points on AIME—it drastically reduces coverage, with agents only attempting 21% of problems. A major failure mode identified was the construction of invalid proofs before they even reached the judge. The results suggest that current verifiers are effective at filtering but struggle with the underlying generation of valid proof steps.
items.bottom_line: The primary bottleneck in automated mathematical reasoning is now the generation of valid proof steps rather than the final verification.

items.title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
items.one_liner: NIBench provides a critical framework for testing the reliability of AI agents in complex, high-stakes scientific workflows like neuroimaging.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced NIBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate autonomous AI agents in the field of neuroimaging. The benchmark assesses agents across three areas: workflow reconstruction across seven tool ecosystems, procedural skill evolution through distillation, and scientific judgment using raw Alzheimer's disease cohort data. Testing 19 language models revealed that while leading agents can follow supplied protocols nearly perfectly, their performance drops significantly without guidance. Furthermore, agents sometimes reach conclusions inconsistent with expert findings, even when given direct access to data.
items.bottom_line: Current AI agents show high proficiency in following neuroimaging protocols but struggle with independent scientific judgment and workflow reconstruction without explicit guidance.

items.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
items.one_liner: A new training-free method for augmenting small engineering datasets significantly improves predictive model accuracy.
items.summary: GenPFN is a new training-free approach for augmenting small tabular datasets in engineering using a pretrained TabPFN classifier. It generates new design candidates by interpolating between successful designs and refining them using classifier gradients. In tests, this method reduced validation mean squared error by 62.1% compared to training on the original small context alone. A case study on ship hull design showed it could produce propeller-compatible candidates with 99.3% accuracy.
items.bottom_line: GenPFN allows engineers to generate high-quality synthetic data for training models even when physical simulation data is extremely limited.

items.title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
items.one_liner: MVDriveBench highlights a critical gap in current MLLM capabilities for multi-view spatio-temporal reasoning in autonomous driving.
items.summary: Researchers have developed MVDriveBench, a new benchmark to test the surround-view video reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in autonomous driving. The study also found a strong correlation between an agent's reasoning performance on the benchmark and its actual closed-loop driving performance in simulations.

items.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
items.one_liner: A new method for editing LLM knowledge prevents 'catastrophic forgetting' during multi-domain updates.
items.summary: MuEdit is a new multi-task editing method for LLMs that addresses the problem of knowledge conflicts when updating models across different domains. The researchers identified that sequential updates often fail because the 'null space' for conflict-free updates shrinks as more tasks are added. MuEdit uses conflict-aware ordering and dynamic low-rank approximation to expand this space and minimize interference. Experiments show it preserves general model capabilities while allowing for effective incremental knowledge updates.
items.bottom_line: MuEdit enables continuous, conflict-free knowledge updates in LLMs by geometrically aligning task-specific updates.

items.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
items.one_liner: A new algorithm makes VLM-based agents safer by considering a set of likely states rather than a single guess.
items.summary: PRaVaSS is a new algorithm designed to improve the reliability of AI agents using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for state estimation. Instead of relying on a single 'best-guess' state, which can lead to unsafe decisions, PRaVaSS constructs a 'Minimal Belief Set' (MBS) that meets a specific confidence threshold. This approach uses the VLM's underlying token distributions to maintain a set of likely states, ensuring computational tractability while enhancing robustness. The method was validated in task-planning pipelines, showing improved decision-making safety.
items.bottom_line: Moving from deterministic 'best-guess' states to probabilistic 'Minimal Belief Sets' significantly improves the safety of agents driven by pretrained perception models.

items.title: Building strong safety evaluations
items.summary: Safety evaluations inform some of the most consequential decisions we make about an AI model, including whether it’s ready to deploy, which safeguards ship alongside it, and what our next round of safety training and research should focus on. items.title: How to hack APIs in 2026
items.summary: Five years is a long time in API security Back in 2021 I wrote a guide on hacking APIs with Farah Hawa. It did well, partly because at that time APIs had become hugely popular in the development world while most cybersecurity content still assumed you were poking at a server-rendered web app. The shift from server rendered to client-side + API is well and truly done now. In 2026 the API is the application for most of what you’ll test. The browser, the mobile app, the smart TV, the partner integration, the AI agent calling a tool, they’re all just clients talking to the same handful of endpoints behind the scenes.

items.one_liner: Understand the grass-roots administrative context and local political friction points in Rajasthan's final phase of panchayat polls.
items.summary: Villagers in 25 districts of Rajasthan cast their votes in the fourth and final phase of the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections, covering 2,524 seats with an estimated 72% voter turnout. The polling experienced disruptions due to electronic voting machine glitches, arrests of individuals attempting to carry mobile phones into booths, and localized boycotts over an irrigation project and reservation anomalies. Counting for all four phases is scheduled for November 20. A total of 8,843 candidates contested this final phase across districts such as Jaipur, Jaisalmer, Baran, and Sikar.
